did_you_know.text: The chapter opens with a description of a fierce storm approaching from the wilderness, like the sandstorms that sweep across the Negev.
The prophet commands Elam and Media to go to war and describes the enemy as a traitor and plunderer.
The intensity of the vision causes the prophet a severe physical and emotional reaction: his loins are filled with trembling, and he is terrified by what he sees and hears.
The feast is disrupted and turned into preparations for war: the table is set, people eat and drink, and then the leaders are told to rise and anoint the shields.
The LORD commands that a watchman be posted, whose task is to watch and report everything he sees.
The watchman must listen with great attentiveness and identify, among other things, a chariot, a pair of horsemen, a chariot drawn by donkeys, and a chariot drawn by camels.
The messenger brings the announcement: “Babylon has fallen, has fallen!” Along with Babylon’s fall, the images of its gods are also shattered and thrown to the ground.
In response to those calling from Seir, the watchman says that morning has come, and night as well, and invites them to return and ask again if they want to inquire further.
The people of Tema are called to help the thirsty fugitives and bring them food, since they have fled from the war.

A precise time prediction is given against Kedar: within one year, counted like a hired worker would count it, its glory will come to an end, and the number of its archers and warriors will be greatly reduced.
